chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and al-Razzaz from Ayoub ibn Nuh and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, all together from Safwan from Muhammad ibn Hakim from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
The woman the likes of whom do not get pregnant, there is no waiting period (iddah) upon her.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (Iddah) for a barren woman after divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a barren woman's iddah is determined by the standard duration of three menstrual cycles or three months, rather than the extended period required for pregnant women. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that the primary purpose of the waiting period is to ascertain lineage, so in the absence of potential pregnancy, the timeline aligns with the general rule for non-pregnant divorcées. It underscores the practical application of Quranic verses in distinguishing between different categories of women during the iddah period.
